 Video: Milan surge into 2-0 lead over Inter within first 10 minutes 
 By Susy Campanale 
 Oct 31, 2026 20:31 
 ITALY - OCTOBER 31: Adrien Rabiot of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammate Diego Moreira during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) 
 Milan got off to an historically good start in the Derby della Madonnina, leading 2-0 within 10 minutes with Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot goals against Inter.
 You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s Serie A games on the Liveblog.

 This match is also being aired live on BBC2 in the UK and on the iPlayer.
 Perfect Milan start to derby
 ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Christian Pulisic of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The Rossoneri could not have asked for a brighter start in this showdown, as Pulisic met the Diego Moreira cross from the right to nod in after three minutes and 45 seconds.
 This was the fastest Rossoneri goal against Inter in Serie A since Alexandre Pato took all of 43 seconds in April 2011.
 A CLOSER LOOK AT PULISIC’S THIRD-MINUTE HEADER! 🇺🇸🔥

 There was another Diego Moreira assist, this time a corner kick routine finding Rabiot to sweep in first-time from 12 yards into the far bottom corner.
 The San Siro is BOUNCING 💥
 Adrien Rabiot scores Milan’s second of the game, and we’re only 11 minutes in 🤯
 Stream Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 https://t.co/lKAI4Z712J
 — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) October 31, 2026 
 No team had been 2-0 up in a Derby della Madonnina within 10 minutes since Inter’s 5-2 victory in 1974, when they scored twice in the first seven minutes.
 ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan interacts with fans during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The Rossoneri side of the city had not celebrated this immediate advantage since 1932, when they still ended up losing 5-4, despite leading 2-0 after six minutes.
 The derby is delivering 🤩
